ui_bugs.issue: Viewer is NOT truly full-screen. Its `position: fixed inset-0` is contained by an ancestor whose CSS `transform` is non-none. Two ancestors have transforms: (1) Modal.jsx inner box uses `animate-fade-up` (index.css keyframe animates `translateY`, with `animation-fill-mode: both` so a residual transform matrix stays) and (2) `<main>` also uses `animate-fade-up`. Per CSS spec, any ancestor with `transform !== none` creates a containing block for `position: fixed` descendants → viewer is trapped to the parent modal (~896x777) instead of the viewport (1920x1080). Visible symptom: dark backdrop covers only the Detail modal area (left sidebar/header still visible), image is clipped, and Playwright reports zoom-in button 'outside of viewport' because the flex-1 content region overflows the constrained fixed container.
ui_bugs.evidence: transformAncestors=[{cls:'relative bg-white rounded-xl … max-h-[90vh] flex flex-…', transform:'matrix(1,0,0,1,0,7.46)'}, {tag:'MAIN', cls:'… animate-fade-up', transform:'matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)'}]; viewer bbox 896x777 vs viewport 1920x1080.
ui_bugs.suggested_fix: Portal the AttachmentViewer to document.body via ReactDOM.createPortal (recommended), OR change `.animate-fade-up` to use opacity-only animation (no transform), OR wrap the viewer in a portal only when opened. Portal is safest and standard for lightbox/fullscreen overlays.

rca of the issue: AttachmentViewer's `position: fixed inset-0 z-[100]` is intended to cover the viewport. However, when rendered as a child of DocumentDetail (which itself lives inside <Modal> and inside <main class='animate-fade-up'>), CSS containing-block rules make `position: fixed` resolve against the nearest ancestor with a non-none `transform`. Both the Modal inner box and <main> apply `animate-fade-up` (keyframe animates `translateY` with fill-mode both), leaving a residual `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,X)`. Result: viewer is confined to the modal box (896x777) instead of the viewport (1920x1080). Standard fix is a React portal to document.body so the overlay escapes any transformed ancestor.
